messages:
jamie: Hey team — we got an external forensics request for raw logs from a customer support escalation. Who owns the process to unlock archived S3 bundles and run a scrub before handing over? cc @sophia @lee

sophia: Short answer: security + legal. Longer: we need a JIT unwrap via KMS-proxy, a scoped SIEM export, and a documented approval in the ticket.

lee: Oncall note: if it's a P0 incident we can accelerate, but standard requests follow the 'archive unlock playbook'. Please paste the ticket template. :point_down: 

jamie: Ticket template I used: 
```
- Requestor: [name]
- Customer: [org]
- Time range: [iso start] -> [iso end]
- Purpose: forensic / legal / support
- Data types: audit, trace, app-logs
- Approver: security lead + legal
- Retention after export: 7d (ephemeral)
```

sophia: Add: review scope to ensure we don't export PCI/SSNs. If anything PII-ish is found, legal decides redaction.

maria: legal here — confirm: exported artifacts must be hashed + checksumed, and we need to record the KMS CMK used for unwrap in the ticket. Also retention window can't exceed 30 days without Legal exec sign-off.

jamie: Noted. Operational question: who runs the actual unwrap? Security-bot or infra? We prefer no long-lived keys in engineer laptops.

security-bot: automated note: KMS-unlock must be performed by the kms-proxy service account (kms-unlock-sa). Manual CMK policy grants require an approved ticket ID.

lee: Exactly — infra ops will call kms-proxy with scoped token. Example command (internal): 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $JIT_TOKEN" -X POST https://kms-proxy.redwood.internal/unlock 
  -d '{"s3_key":"s3://archive/2025/05/01/bundle.gz","ticket":"#2809876543"}'
```

jamie: After unlock, we should stream directly to a scrubber lambda that masks email/SSN and writes to a temp bucket with server-side encryption. Anyone object?

sophia: No objections. Add a policy: scrubbed exports are available for max 7 days, then auto-delete. Any access must be via presigned URL one-time use.

maria: Legal: require a preservation log entry in the legal tracker for any export tied to a compliance request. Also capture approver signature (slack thread ok).

lee: Security practical: enforce RBAC so only members of "forensics-team" group + ticket approver can request the presigned URL. We'll add an audit event: export.request, kms.unwrap, scrub.run, presign.generate.

jamie: Good. Last q: SIEM export — do we send raw events to their SIEM or push scrubbed CSV? Customer asks for Splunk ingestion.

sophia: Never send raw events without redaction. For Splunk ingestion we provide a scrubbed event stream (JSONL) via HTTPS endpoint. We should also rate-limit and put a TTL.

security-bot: policy reminder: any external export must set metadata: {"export_type":"scrubbed","ticket":"#2809876543","expires_at":"2025-06-01T12:00:00Z","kms_key":"alias/redwood-escrow"}.

jamie: I'll draft the playbook changes and a concise checklist. Will post PR to infra-runbooks and update the ticket with approvals. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
